Girdwood Housing and Economic Committee
                              Oct 7, 2026
                             Regular Meeting
                              Minutes Draft
         6 p.m. via Microsoft Teams & Girdwood Community Room

This hybrid meeting is taking place via Microsoft Teams & at the Girdwood Community Room, 250 Egloff Rd:

All committees of the GBOS operate under the Girdwood Public Meetings Standards of Conduct.

From 6PM-6:20PM the group has 3 members. Without a quorum, group did introductions with new prospective
member, whose nomination will be considered by GBOS on FRI at their Special Meeting.


Call to Order 6:20 p.m. Krystal Hoke, co-chair
Roll Call: Erin Eker (EE); Brooks Chander (BC); Matt Schechter (MS); Krystal Hoke (KH)
Quorum confirmed.
Tim Cabana (TC) arrives at 6:45

Agenda Revisions and Approval
Oct 7 2026 meeting agenda approved                   BC/MS        Assent
August 5 2026 & Sept 9 meeting minutes approved         BC/MS        Assent

GBOS report: GBOS GHEC Liaison: Kellie Okonek is unable to attend, Jennifer Wingard is attending.

Announcements/Presentations:
GHEC meetings will be held on WED Oct 7, Nov 4 and Dec 2. They will return to 1st MON monthly in 2027.

PUBLIC COMMENT:
Hoke: Prior to achieving quorum, group discussed that Holtan Hills reservations for lots opened and closed since the
last GHEC meeting.

Mike Edgington: Applied for appointment to GHEC in August. Item has not been voted on by GBOS as it was moved
but not seconded. He remains interested in serving on committee and plans to participate as public.

Tuttle: Items promoted by GHEC to GBOS and approved have been detrimental to her business and business owners
in Girdwood in general.

Old Business:
     1.  Housing Study RFP update and follow-up (Kelley): No update
     2. GHEC Advance the Housing Policies from the GCP-
        POLICY H4.4: Develop an appropriate property tax incentive programs to implement in Girdwood.
GHEC programs for review are derived from the Girdwood Comprehensive Plan, which was approved by the
community and subsequently by the Assembly. Support for the concepts in the plan for property tax exemptions to
help stimulate change in housing availability should provide support for programs based upon them. In addition,
GBOS Supervisor Okonek encourage specific concepts for GBOS to pursue, which is what Brooks has brought to this
meeting. It may be possible to layer some of these approaches to further incentivize property owners to rent to
workforce renters, conversely, there may need to be language to cap the total amount of exemption. Tax relief could
be in the form of reduction of GVSA tax via rebate, credit on upcoming year, etc. MOA legal dept would draft actual
ordinances and they would be brought back to Girdwood for review. As programs have synergy with each other, they
will be held at GHEC until all that pass are ready to go to GBOS together.





        Meeting Agendas and minutes are available: Municipal Road Maintenance Service Areas gbos-hes

                                                                                         1

Program 1: STR to LTR Conversion through property tax exemption of local service area tax.

Motion:
GHEC moves to approve Program 1, a tax exemption to encourage conversion from Short Term Rental to Long Term
Rental, as presented.
Motion by BC/EE
Group discusses various aspects of the proposal and finds that they need a fuller idea of implementation, oversight,
impacts to the local property tax base and estimate of the possible amount that property owners would receive as
incentive. Motion is withdrawn. Item will return with additional information


Program 2: Extension of existing code provision for 8 unit (minimum) multi-family developments for an additional 5
years.

Motion:
GHEC moves to approve Program 2, allowing GVSA to extend the existing program for 5 years (to 25 from 20).
Motion by BC/EE
Motion carries 4-0 in roll call vote, with 1 (TC) abstaining.

This program is already available for developers in Girdwood, the action would extend the horizon to 25 years instead
of the current end of 20 years.
Group discusses that making it applicable to smaller developments, like 4 units, would be more beneficial in Girdwood.
There are questions about whether this requires that the occupier uses the unit as a primary residence.

Program 3: Workforce Housing Property Tax Exemption

Motion:
GHEC moves to approve Program 3, a workforce housing property tax exemption.
Motion by BC/EE

Group discusses that this program would require change of state statute and then require new municipal code to bring
to fruition.
Item is postponed to future meeting.

Program 4: Low Income Rental Property Exemption

Motion:
GHEC moves to approve Program 4, an exemption to encourage long term rental to those who qualify as low income
through tax incentive.
Motion by BC/MS
Motion carries 5-0 in roll call vote

Group discusses that this program and program 1 are could be related and could combine to help retain and stimulate
long term rental to lower income/workforce. Group discusses AMI compared to market rate of rental in Girdwood.
GHEC will continue to work on Program 1 and possibly Program 3 and when determination is made on those, will pass
them to GBOS.

     3.  Review Holtan Hills HOA Bylaws: Not yet received.

New Business:
     4.  Workforce Housing Definition (Schechter/Hoke)
Review of definitions of Workforce Housing and related topic of Qualifying Local Employment.
Items will return to the next agenda for vote.

     5.  Glacier Creek Valley Economy and Local Businesses (Amanda Tuttle)
Amanda Tuttle expresses frustration that local government has not taken action on items that she has brought
forward at the local, state and federal level, which impact the local housing situation and economy.
Impact to Old Girdwood homes and businesses from dike, drainage and flooding
Water concerns due to lack of city water service in Old Girdwood and reliance on shallow wells.
Lack of understanding that the local economy is in dire condition
Reliance on Resort’s observations of housing and economy without input from other local businesses
                                                                                         2

Inability for businesses to survive in Girdwood
Disregard for Old Girdwood compared to the rest of the community, which much of the commercial benefit and local
housing is in Old Girdwood.

When asked for a specific item that GHEC can help to push forward, Amanda requests support for Watershed Study.
One member observes that this could be added to the work plan for GHEC in 2027.

Program Updates: Not discussed
     6.  Reports from Subcommittee groups:
       RFP draft language for Orca Mtn View Subdivision land disposal (Chandler/Eker/Yelle) Start mid-Nov.
     7.  Update on housing projects under way, if any
     8.  Parcels requested for transfer:
          6-076: Across Karolius, adjacent to California Creek Park (to GCLT)
          6-039: Along Alyeska Highway/Across Ruane Road from the Industrial Park
           6-011(C): Formerly 6—016;6.5 acre portion only within Holtan Hills now GIP.
          6-134: Across Karolius from 6-076. This parcel is under consideration for the RV park (to GPR)
     9.  Discuss any updates to program matrix and data collection on short-term housing (Schechter)
       STR data from MOA registration

Next meeting: Nov 4 2026
Adjourn 8:20PM
